text: The Earth just stopped spinning for one second. Here's what happens to you.
At the equator, the ground under you spins east at about a thousand miles an hour.
You don't feel it, because you, the air, and the oceans all move with it.
Then the ground stops. But you don't.
You keep flying east at a thousand miles an hour. That's faster than the speed of sound.
So does anything not bolted to bedrock. Cars, trees, even houses.
The air keeps going too, with winds three times faster than the strongest tornado ever measured.
The oceans slam into the coasts as giant tsunamis.
The safest spot? Right at the North or South Pole, where the ground barely moves.
And that's what happens if the Earth stops spinning for one second.
